statement: Novgorod's relationship with the Golden Horde was indirect and episodic: the Mongols did not physically invade Novgorod (1237–1240) though they burned other cities, but they sent census-takers and tax collectors periodically. Alexander Nevsky — Prince of Novgorod and then Grand Prince of Vladimir — negotiated the tribute relationship with the Horde, accepting Mongol financial sovereignty while maintaining Novgorodian self-government. The 'anti-Mongol' riots in Novgorod (1257–1259), when census-takers arrived, were suppressed by Alexander Nevsky himself to preserve the tribute accommodation.
